components.component: native determinant Frechet derivative / Jacobi formula
components.proof_and_scope: Global differentiability is proved from the native determinant Leibniz formula. The exact polynomial expansion at the identity computes its derivative; factorization through an invertible X and uniqueness of genuine derivative identify the native fderiv. IsUnit(det X) is exactly invertibility.

For actual SPD X, the native Frechet differential of trace X-log(det X)-n is U |-> trace((1-X inverse)U). In the manuscript symmetric affine coordinates this is the gradient 1-X inverse under the trace pairing. A stronger det-nonzero lemma supplies the local ambient extension needed by the second derivative.

Native Ring.inverse differentiation is transported to the actual nonsingular matrix inverse. The actual derivative of the specified trace-coordinate gradient map is U |-> X inverse U X inverse; no derivative of a candidate is assumed.

The derivative of Y |-> (fderiv matrixPotential Y)(U), evaluated at X in direction V, is trace(X inverse V X inverse U). A genuine HasFDerivAt proof transfers through eventual equality on the open det-nonzero neighborhood. Cyclic trace gives the exact manuscript order trace(X inverse U X inverse V), independently compiled for symmetric tangents in SigmaFinalIndependentAudit.manuscript_matrix_hessian.

The Bregman expression uses the native fderiv of matrixPotential itself. Substitution into the separately proved algebraic identity gives trace(Y inverse X)-log(det(Y inverse X))-n for actual SPD X,Y.

representation_notes: All calculus uses native finite real Matrix, native determinant/inverse, HasFDerivAt/fderiv, and the Frobenius normed-ring/algebra topology. The same local instances are activated in the independently compiled audit.

The potential is extended to all matrices via Real.log(det X), which agrees with the draft on SPD matrices. The local det-nonzero extension supports ambient differentiation without requiring the SPD cone to be open in the full matrix space.

The displayed gradient is certified through its trace-pairing differential, rather than a separately bundled native Riesz-gradient operator. At SPD X the matrix 1-X inverse is symmetric, so its trace pairing with symmetric tangents is the manuscript affine pairing.

The Hessian is encoded as the actual Frechet derivative of the first derivative evaluated at a fixed U. Its proof establishes derivative existence by HasFDerivAt; it is not merely a formula obtained by naming a gradient. The independent audit verifies symmetry/order of U,V in the manuscript.
No positivity is claimed on nonsymmetric tangents; the manuscript metric lives on symmetric tangents. The derivative formulas being valid on the larger ambient matrix space do not change that domain.
M3 geodesics and M4 Gaussian/Wishart realizations are outside this module and remain unaffected.
